items.readable_text:
Content:
We can use logarithms to solve equations where the variable is in an exponent.
For instance, suppose we are given the equation
[MATH: {\color{blue}2}^x=5.]

Content:
Notice that the base of the exponential is [MATH: {\color{blue}2}.] So, if we take [MATH: \log_{\color{blue}2}] of both sides of the equation, we have that
[MATH: \log_{2} (2^{x})|= \log_{2} (5).]

Content:
Now, we can use the fact that [MATH: \log_{\color{blue}b} \left( {\color{blue}b}^c \right) = c] to simplify the left-hand side. This gives
[MATH: x = \log_{\color{blue}2} (5).]

Content:
This is the solution! We often present the solution of an exponential equation as an exact solution in logarithmic form.

Content:
Note that when taking the [MATH: \log_b] of both sides of an exponential equation, we always use the base of the exponential as the base of the logarithm.

sections.normalized_html: Find the exact solution of the equation [MATH: 2^{x+1}=3.]
sections.readable_text: Find the exact solution of the equation [MATH: 2^{x+1}=3.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we take [MATH: \log_2] of both sides of the equation:

[MATH: 2^{x + 1}|= 3; \log_{2} (2^{x + 1})|= \log_{2} (3)]

Now, we use the fact that [MATH: \log_b \left( b^c \right) = c] to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

[MATH: x+1 = \log_2 \left( 3 \right).]

Finally, we solve for [MATH: x,] as follows:

[MATH: x + 1|= \log_{2} (3); x|= \log_{2} (3) − 1]

Therefore, the solution is [MATH: x= \log_2 \left( 3 \right) - 1.]

sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: 3^{2x+3}=5,] find the value of [MATH: x] rounded to [MATH: 3] decimal places.
sections.readable_text: Given that [MATH: 3^{2x+3}=5,] find the value of [MATH: x] rounded to [MATH: 3] decimal places.

sections.normalized_html:
Taking [MATH: \log_3] of both sides of the equation, we get

[MATH: \eqalign{ 3^{2x+3} &= 5 \[3pt] \log_3 \left(3^{2x+3}\right) &= \log_3 (5) \[3pt] 2x+3 &= \log_3 (5) . \[3pt] }]

Then, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula and solve for [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: 2x + 3|= (\log (5))/(\log (3)); 2x|= (\log (5))/(\log (3)) − 3; x|= (\log (5))/(2\log (3)) − (3)/(2)]

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives [MATH: x \approx -0.768] rounded to [MATH: 3] decimal places.

Note: We used the change of base formula to rewrite the right-hand side, as many calculators can only compute base [MATH: 10] logarithms.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can use logarithms to solve equations where the variable is in an exponent.
For instance, suppose we are given the equation
[MATH: {\color{blue}2}^x=5.]

Content:
Notice that the base of the exponential is [MATH: {\color{blue}2}.] So, if we take [MATH: \log_{\color{blue}2}] of both sides of the equation, we have that
[MATH: \log_{2} (2^{x})|= \log_{2} (5).]

Content:
Now, we can use the fact that [MATH: \log_{\color{blue}b} \left( {\color{blue}b}^c \right) = c] to simplify the left-hand side. This gives
[MATH: x = \log_{\color{blue}2} (5).]

Content:
This is the solution! We often present the solution of an exponential equation as an exact solution in logarithmic form.

Content:
Note that when taking the [MATH: \log_b] of both sides of an exponential equation, we always use the base of the exponential as the base of the logarithm.

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using Logarithms

Example Prompt:
Find the exact solution of the equation [MATH: 2^{x+1}=3.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we take [MATH: \log_2] of both sides of the equation:

[MATH: 2^{x + 1}|= 3; \log_{2} (2^{x + 1})|= \log_{2} (3)]

Now, we use the fact that [MATH: \log_b \left( b^c \right) = c] to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

[MATH: x+1 = \log_2 \left( 3 \right).]

Finally, we solve for [MATH: x,] as follows:

[MATH: x + 1|= \log_{2} (3); x|= \log_{2} (3) − 1]

Therefore, the solution is [MATH: x= \log_2 \left( 3 \right) - 1.]

Item 5 — Example: Finding Approximate Solutions to Exponential Equations Using Logarithms

Example Prompt:
Given that [MATH: 3^{2x+3}=5,] find the value of [MATH: x] rounded to [MATH: 3] decimal places.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Taking [MATH: \log_3] of both sides of the equation, we get

[MATH: \eqalign{
3^{2x+3} &= 5 \[3pt]
\log_3 \left(3^{2x+3}\right)	&= \log_3 (5) \[3pt]
2x+3 &= \log_3 (5) . \[3pt]
}]

Then, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula and solve for [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: 2x + 3|= (\log (5))/(\log (3)); 2x|= (\log (5))/(\log (3)) − 3; x|= (\log (5))/(2\log (3)) − (3)/(2)]

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives
[MATH: x \approx -0.768]
rounded to [MATH: 3] decimal places.

Note: We used the change of base formula to rewrite the right-hand side, as many calculators can only compute base [MATH: 10] logarithms.
